questions.prompt: Which statement about the beneficial environmental roles of microorganisms is FALSE?

options.text: Cyanobacteria perform photosynthesis and release oxygen.
Bacteria and fungi act as decomposers, recycling nutrients.
All microorganisms in the environment are harmful pathogens.
Anabaena variabilis is an example of a cyanobacterium.
Photosynthesis converts CO2 + H2O into glucose + O2.

questions.explanation: False. Most microorganisms are not harmful; many play beneficial environmental roles.

questions.prompt: Which organism is fermented to produce leavened bread and alcoholic beverages?
How does Lactobacillus acidophilus benefit human health?
questions.explanation: It produces lactic acid, is a normal/beneficial resident of the vaginal environment, and acts as a probiotic that helps prevent yeast infections.

questions.prompt: Genetic engineering, a form of biotechnology, involves:

options.text: Manipulating genes so an organism produces a desired protein
Classifying organisms by genus and species

questions.explanation: Manipulating genes so an organism produces a desired protein.

questions.prompt: When was the Golden Age of Microbiology, and what four questions did scientists try to answer during it?
questions.explanation: Mid-1800s to early 1900s (~50 years). Questions: Does life arise spontaneously? What causes fermentation? What causes disease? How can disease be prevented/treated?

questions.prompt: Which statement about the theory of spontaneous generation is FALSE?

options.text: It proposed that life could arise from non-living matter.
Spallanzani’s sealed-flask experiment supported the theory.
Pasteur’s swan-necked flask experiment helped disprove the theory.
Redi suspected microorganisms could cause meat spoilage.
The theory was ultimately shown to be incorrect.

questions.explanation: False. The sealed flask showed NO growth, supporting the idea that microbes come from outside (contamination), not spontaneous generation.

questions.prompt: In Spallanzani’s experiment, what happened in the SEALED, boiled flask?
Describe how Pasteur’s swan-necked flask experiment differed from Spallanzani’s experiment, and why the design mattered.
questions.explanation: Pasteur used a swan-necked flask instead of a sealed one. Air could enter (addressing the “vital force” objection), but gravity trapped incoming microorganisms in the curve of the neck, so the broth stayed sterile — proving microorganisms in the air, not the air itself, caused contamination.

questions.prompt: Pasteur’s fermentation work showed that fermentation is caused by:

options.text: A chemical reaction with no living organisms involved

questions.prompt: Explain how Pasteur’s work on fermentation helped lead to the Germ Theory of Disease.
questions.explanation: Pasteur showed that specific living microorganisms (yeast) cause a specific effect (fermentation), and bacteria cause spoilage. This established that living microbes could cause specific biological changes, providing the conceptual foundation that microbes could likewise cause disease.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Germ Theory of Disease is FALSE?

options.text: Louis Pasteur proposed that microorganisms could cause disease.
Robert Koch performed the rigorous experimental proof.
Alexander Fleming co-developed the theory with Pasteur.
It followed directly from earlier fermentation/spoilage research.

questions.explanation: False. Pasteur and Koch developed the Germ Theory; Fleming discovered penicillin (unrelated to developing the theory itself).

questions.prompt: Who emphasized the importance of hand washing to prevent disease spread?
Match each scientist to his/her contribution toward combatting microorganisms: Ignaz Semmelweis, Florence Nightingale, Joseph Lister, Alexander Fleming.
questions.explanation: Semmelweis — hand washing. Nightingale — hospital cleanliness. Lister — germicides. Fleming — discovered Penicillin (first antibiotic).

questions.prompt: Alexander Fleming is credited with discovering:
What is the difference between an enzyme and an antibiotic, and who is credited with discovering each in the context of this module?
questions.explanation: An enzyme is a protein that catalyzes chemical reactions (discovered in fermentation by Eduard Buchner); an antibiotic is a substance that kills/inhibits bacteria (the first, Penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming).
